correctness.rationale: Proof explicitly decomposes the zero-sum quadratic form into sibling, interbranch and radial sectors. The radial-vs-interbranch matrix difference is a strictly positive Laplace-Gram form for \(1<p<2\), forcing the first singularity to be radial; strict-downward inheritance gives exact endpoint uniqueness. The scalar determinant root is in the stated open interval and has a one-dimensional nullspace; centered Gram rank follows. Uniform Taylor expansion proves the diagonal \(b^{-2}\) limit. The extracted standalone checker passed 600 exact identities, 30 numerical critical inertias and high-precision limit diagnostics; they corroborate rather than replace the analytic argument.

value.rationale: A natural complete radius-two family of finite spherically symmetric trees, previously treated numerically and by bounds, receives a two-parameter exact negative-type classification, sharp endpoint Hilbert dimension and an explicit inverse-square branching law. The universal Gram domination mechanism and uniform scaling offer a reusable model for deeper trees, beyond isolated small-matrix recomputation.
